problem: Traditional SLAM-based navigation lacks semantics, and zero-shot navigation with LLMs/VLMs is hampered by how the LLM's general knowledge is turned into perception and path planning through suitable spatial representations. The paper reviews the open challenges: knowledge transfer, perceptual uncertainty, multimodal fusion, and decision interpretability.
motivation: Zero-shot navigation lets embodied agents work in unfamiliar environments without task-specific training. Foundation models supply semantic and generalized knowledge, but their usefulness depends on the spatial representation they are paired with. A systematic comparison of these representations is needed to guide design.
key_idea: Survey LLM-based zero-shot navigation and compare spatial representations, then propose a hybrid paradigm combining universal spatial representations with continual learning and human-robot collaboration.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations or experiments can be cited. The abstract's claim is that the choice of spatial representation is the bridge between LLM knowledge and actionable perception and planning.
method: Systematic analysis: reviews how LLMs are applied in zero-shot navigation.
Comparative evaluation: compares spatial representation techniques.
Hybrid paradigm (proposed): integrates universal spatial representations with continual learning and human-robot collaboration.
